newsitem.title: USA: Japan trade not central issue at Denver meet - Rubin.
newsitem.headline: Japan trade not central issue at Denver meet - Rubin.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin denied on Saturday that the United States was toning down its criticism of Japan over Tokyo's rising trade surplus, but he admitted the issue was not the main focus of meetings here.
"I don't think that issue was downplayed or up-played," Rubin told reporters here for the summit of industrial nations.
But he said that there was "no reason" why Japan's trade position should have been the central issue of either the summit or a separate bilateral meeting on Thursday between Tokyo and Washington.
"I don't think there was any expectation that this would be a central issue," Rubin said. "There was no reason why it should have been."
The Japanese government reported earlier this week that the country's customs-cleared trade surplus soared by more than 200 percent in May from a year earlier.
In a statement issued on Saturday, G7 leaders said Japan needed to achieve strong domestic demand-led economic growth and avoid a significant increase in its trade surplus.
"We continue to feel that's very important for Japan, very important for the rest of the world," Rubin said.
Japan believes it is on its way to accomplishing that objective through its program of deregulation, Rubin noted.
"Deregulation is very good for Japan, very good for the rest of the world," he said.

"If it accomplishes that objective, despite the rapid rate of (budget) deficit reduction, then that objective would have been satisifed. If not, then they have the challenge of meeting that objective," Rubin added.
